trials.claim: Each code limited to 5,000 monthly requests and 20 locations
trials.claimQuote: Each code comes with just 2 limitations: 5,000 monthly requests and 20 locations per account.
trials.reasoning: The seller said there are just two limitations, but E1 reports an additional forced restriction to use the CNAMEs the vendor wants for agency setup.

exhibits.quote: I wanted to like this for its simplicity until I got to the agency setup. You'll be forced to use cnames that they want.
exhibits.argument: Quote shows an additional forced-CNAME restriction beyond the claimed just two limitations.

trials.claim: 5 codes gives 100 locations for agency growth
trials.claimQuote: You get 100 locations (that's 100 single-location clients) to grow your agency.
trials.reasoning: E2 vaguely says users may eventually offload clients or pay more, but it does not dispute that 5 codes provide 100 locations.

exhibits.quote: As eventually you'll either have to offload clients or pay them more to keep them all there.
exhibits.argument: Quote reports monthly limits force offloading clients or paying more, undermining 100-location agency growth.

trials.claim: Resource-intensive new features may require own API key or third-party service
trials.claimQuote: Yes. If a new feature is resource-intensive, we'll give you the option to add your own API key or connect a third-party service under your own account.
trials.reasoning: No exhibits were admitted for this claim, so there is no evidence either way about API keys or third-party services for resource-intensive features.

trials.claim: AI system automatically gets more five star reviews
trials.claimQuote: AI reputation management that gets you more five star reviews, automatically.
trials.reasoning: Two buyers report Google reviews skyrocketing and the product being useful for getting additional reviews; E3's note that some visitors do not finish a review does not materially undercut those results.

exhibits.quote: I have it directed to my google review site but I find many people only click the face and dont fill out the google review.
exhibits.argument: Quote shows visitors click but do not complete Google reviews, undermining automatically getting more five-star reviews.

exhibits.quote: I'm using it at the hair salon, and google reviews are skyrockeitng!
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms real-world use produced skyrocketing Google reviews.

exhibits.quote: The product is very useful for getting additional reviews, which is a huge key to increasing the ROI for local businesses.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms the product is useful for getting additional reviews for businesses.

trials.claim: 5 codes required to unlock agency white label plan
trials.claimQuote: You need 5 codes to unlock the agency white label plan.
trials.reasoning: E7 and E8 confirm white-label use at a high tier and through a custom domain, but neither exhibit states that 5 codes are required to unlock it.

exhibits.quote: I got the highest tier and I'm using More Good Reviews for both myself and my clients (under our white label name - Glowsay
exhibits.argument: Highest-tier buyer confirms using the product under their own white label name for clients.

exhibits.quote: There is very detailed documentation and the ability to white-label through my own domain is amazing.
exhibits.argument: Agency-level buyer confirms white-label through own domain works as promised.

trials.claim: All features including integrations, API and MCP with every code
trials.claimQuote: Yes. You get all features included with every code, including integrations, API, and MCP access.
trials.reasoning: E4 says the product lacks an unnamed feature, but does not identify it or show that integrations, API, or MCP are missing from any code.

exhibits.quote: More Good Reviews is superior and more polished than these competitors, but lacks this feature.
exhibits.argument: Quote reports the product lacks a requested feature, contradicting that all features are included.
